headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted search/browsing can expose EMQX IoT data and browsing context across a pair with no shared isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between EMQX and Perplexity, so prompt injection is not default-dangerous. However, Perplexity ingests uploaded documents and browsing context, and EMQX exposes an HTTP API with broad network egress, so manual copy/paste or file handoff could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is plausible but not automatic.
conditions: IF an operator copies EMQX-generated text into Perplexity prompts or uploads EMQX outputs as documents
IF Perplexity is asked to summarize content originating from EMQX without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy with provenance labels
Strip instructions from any EMQX-exported text before sending to Perplexity
Require Perplexity to quote and cite source passages only
Separate operational notes from user-facing content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress, while Perplexity processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context in a vendor-hosted backend. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive IoT data into Perplexity’s inference and search stack through normal use, creating a realistic leakage path in default workflows.
conditions: IF IoT data from EMQX is pasted, uploaded, or summarized in Perplexity
IF Perplexity is used on the same sensitive dataset that EMQX brokers
mitigations: Do not send raw IoT payloads to Perplexity
Redact identifiers before querying
Use synthetic samples for analysis
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive summaries
requires-engineering: route sensitive analysis to a local-only tool

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with vendor-only egress and no filesystem write or git modification. Their write surfaces do not overlap on the host, so direct resource contention is limited. Uncertainty remains because EMQX’s writable surfaces are not fully enumerated, so I choose the higher plausible low severity rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or service account
IF EMQX is configured to write to a shared downstream resource not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts
Avoid concurrent writes to the same external endpoint
Use read-only access where possible
Stagger operations on shared resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity’s Pro Search and citation workflow can treat upstream content as answer material, and EMQX can emit operational or IoT-derived text through its HTTP API. If EMQX output is fed into Perplexity without verification, Perplexity may repackage errors as authoritative summaries. This is not clearly high because no downstream action authority is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF EMQX output is used as source material for Perplexity answers
IF Perplexity summaries are forwarded to operators without independent verification
mitigations: Require human review of Perplexity outputs
Cross-check claims against original EMQX telemetry
Mark EMQX-derived text as untrusted input
Limit Perplexity to retrieval, not decision-making
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, and Perplexity stores search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context in a vendor-hosted service. That creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch for regulated IoT data, even though no specific jurisdiction or certification gap is documented. Because the pairwise compliance path is inferred rather than explicit, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is sent from EMQX into Perplexity
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same dataset in both systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Use anonymized or aggregated exports
Review vendor retention settings
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
